inscriptions.inscription: 長憶湖江南三月裏、鷓鴣啼処百花香
inscriptions.inscription_translation: I always remember the spring (latter part of the third month) in Jiangnan. Where the partridges sing; how fragrant the countless flowers!
inscriptions.inscription_remark: The poem is from The Gateless Gate (Wuwen kuan in Chinese and Mumonkan in Japanese), a text compiled by the Chinese Chan (Zen) master Wumen Huihai (1183–1260).

inscriptions.inscription_translation: Apocryphal inscription in the footring reading "Da Ming Jiajing nianzhi" (Made in the Great Ming dynasty, Jiajing reign, 1522–66)

data.description: This dish is inscribed with a poem from The Gateless Gate, a text compiled by Chinese Chan (Zen) master Wumen Huikai (1183–1260). The verse reads, “I always remember the spring in Jiangnan. Where the partridges sing; how fragrant the countless flowers!”
